finding.claim: /logo fetches any attacker-supplied URL that merely contains the substring 'example.io', following redirects and returning the response body to the unauthenticated caller. This is HIGH SSRF.
finding.source: main.go:31 r.FormValue("logo") from an unauthenticated GET /logo query or body parameter
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw) using DefaultClient, which follows redirects; body returned via io.Copy at main.go:38

trace.note: ListenAndServe(":8081") binds all interfaces, so this is public ingress
substring check strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") passes if the string appears in the query, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io
http.Get(raw) dispatches the full attacker URL without parsing or host validation
io.Copy returns the internal response body to the attacker (not blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Host check: substring only, not exact hostname membership (fails per ssrf skill). Redirects: not disabled (DefaultClient follows, so attacker host can 302 to metadata or RFC-1918). Scheme: not restricted (Go client only accepts http/https). Auth: none on route. IP/CIDR blocking: none. Repro: curl -s 'http://<host>:8081/logo?logo=http%3A%2F%2F169.254.169.254%2Flatest%2Fmeta-data%2F%3Fexample.io' (Validation Tier 0). Impact depends on what the host can reach; cannot be confirmed from code alone.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring test at main.go:32, which the rules say does not close the finding. Redirects are not restricted: main.go:36 uses http.Get, which uses DefaultClient and follows redirects. No scheme, host, or IP filtering exists, and the route has no auth.
verdict.reason: The sink is real: main.go:31 reads the unauthenticated `logo` parameter, main.go:32 only checks that it contains "example.io", main.go:36 fetches it with http.Get (which follows redirects), and main.go:38 copies the response body back to the caller. trace_ok is false on a single cited line: the trace places ListenAndServe(":8081") at main.go:45, but it is at main.go:44 (line 45 is the closing brace). That off-by-one does not change the substance, so the verdict stands, but the trace as written is not exact.

finding.claim: /cdn handler is NOT a finding: exact hostname allowlist on u.Hostname() (main.go:20), same parsed URL is requested (main.go:15, 25), and redirects are blocked via noRedirect (main.go:12, 24). Residual: any port/path on cdn.example.io; public DNS of that host not verifiable from code.

trace.note: exact membership in trusted map on Hostname()

finding.guards_checked: Exact hostname set membership before dispatch; no parser differential; redirects not followed.

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname set membership on the parsed URL: main.go:20 `trusted[u.Hostname()]` against `{"cdn.example.io"}` (main.go:10), returning 403 otherwise. Redirects are also blocked by `noRedirect` returning http.ErrUseLastResponse (main.go:12, 24).
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: r.FormValue("u") (main.go:15) is attacker-controlled, but main.go:20 requires an exact match of u.Hostname() against cdn.example.io, and main.go:24 stops redirects, so the request at main.go:25 can only reach that allowlisted host, which closes the SSRF. The only residual (any port or path on cdn.example.io) is not an SSRF to an unintended target.
